title: Surgical Management and Drainage Outcomes in Acute Obstructive Pyelonephritis: Ureteral Stenting vs. Percutaneous Nephrostomy in a Retrospective Tertiary-Care Cohort
content: When a bacterial infection of the upper urinary tract coexists with mechanical urinary obstruction, it is known as acute obstructive pyelonephritis (AOP), an urgent urological emergency. Antimicrobial therapy alone is insufficient unless the obstructed collecting system is rapidly decompressed. This retrospective study assessed the surgical profile of patients with AOP, emphasizing the etiology of obstruction, imaging severity, timing of urine drainage, and early outcomes after percutaneous nephrostomy or retrograde ureteral stenting. In 62% of cases, urolithiasis was the most common cause of obstruction. The next most frequent causes were tumors, benign prostatic hyperplasia, ureteral stenosis, and other causes. Forty-four patients underwent retrograde ureteral stenting, and fifty-six underwent percutaneous nephrostomy. The mean time from admission to drainage was 27.6 ± 7.9 hours. Imaging showed that 32% of pa-tients had pyonephrosis, and 14% had bilateral involvement. Overall, 17% of cases involved urosepsis, 17% involved acute renal injury, 22% involved critical care unit hospitalization, and 1% involved in-hospital mortality. During the first 72 hours, both drainage techniques were associated with a gradual improvement in inflammatory markers. Short-term outcomes did not differ between drainage groups. The choice of decompression approach was guided by anatomical feasibility, obstruction severity, and clinician judgment. Manage AOP as a source-control emergency. In this cohort, both percutaneous nephrostomy and ureteral stenting were used effectively for urgent decompression. Individualize the drainage route based on the obstruction mechanism, imaging findings, clinical stability, and technical feasibility. These findings support a surgery-centered approach to managing AOP that integrates imaging, drainage timing, and early biological response.
